supportingEvidence.title: Reuters: IRGC says Iran and Oman reached Hormuz share and revenue agreements
supportingEvidence.note: Reuters reports an IRGC spokesperson, citing semi-official Tasnim, said Iran and Oman reached agreements concerning their share of the Strait of Hormuz and its revenues. The spokesperson also said U.S. interference had delayed negotiations.

supportingEvidence.title: Oman Foreign Ministry: established Hormuz navigation coordination background
supportingEvidence.note: Primary Omani background confirms that Oman has been engaged in formal navigation-management and temporary-corridor coordination around Hormuz. It supports the existence of the negotiating channel, but does not independently confirm the newly reported revenue/share terms.

supportingEvidence.title: Reuters/Kpler: physical Hormuz traffic remains depressed
supportingEvidence.note: Only five commodity vessels transited on Aug. 25 versus a 10-day average of 15, so any governance agreement has not yet translated into normal observed commercial flow.

contradictingEvidence.title: Reuters: current agreement claim is one-sided
contradictingEvidence.note: The fresh share/revenue agreement is currently attributed to an Iranian Revolutionary Guards spokesperson through Tasnim. No matching Omani primary announcement was found in this cycle, so exact terms and implementation status remain unconfirmed.

contradictingEvidence.title: Reuters/Kpler: throughput has not normalized
contradictingEvidence.note: Observed commodity-vessel traffic remains roughly one-third of the recent average, which contradicts any interpretation that a governance agreement by itself means operational reopening.

falsifier: Downgrade or supersede this claim if Oman publicly denies the reported share/revenue agreement, if subsequent official texts show the terms remain unresolved, or if no observable implementation appears in navigation rules, fees/revenues, vessel permissions or commercial flows. Upgrade only after Omani primary confirmation and measurable operational effects.

evidence.title: Reuters report on claimed Iran-Oman Hormuz share/revenue agreement

title: Iran claims Hormuz talks reached governance and revenue-sharing terms
summary: An IRGC spokesperson says Iran and Oman reached agreements over their share of the Strait of Hormuz and its revenues. This would move the negotiation from temporary passage toward chokepoint governance, but Oman has not yet independently confirmed the new terms and observed commercial traffic remains severely depressed.
delta: Upgrade the Hormuz state from corridor-only negotiations to CLAIMED_GOVERNANCE_AGREEMENT, but keep operational status at CONTESTED_REOPENING. Preserve the source asymmetry: political/governance terms may be advancing faster than physical shipping recovery and remain pending Omani confirmation.
firstOrderImpacts: potential clarification or change in navigation authority, fees, revenue allocation and vessel-access rules if the agreement is confirmed
continued shipping and insurance caution because physical throughput remains weak despite political progress
greater sensitivity of Gulf shipping contracts and routing to implementation details rather than diplomatic headlines alone
secondOrderImpacts: a confirmed revenue-sharing framework would turn chokepoint control into a measurable economic-rights layer for the Orbital Insight graph
shipping intelligence should track governance claims separately from physical flow and commercial compliance
the broader Nexus resource-access-rights thesis gains a live geopolitical case where control, permission and revenue may be jointly negotiated

alphaHunter.hypothesis: Implementation telemetry will reveal whether the claimed Hormuz governance agreement is real before political narratives converge.
alphaHunter.baseline: public Iran/Oman diplomatic statements and crude-price reaction
alphaHunter.alternativeData: independent vessel throughput, permission/blacklist changes, port notices, tanker freight and war-risk insurance, evidence of toll/revenue collection, and refined-product delivery data
alphaHunter.incrementalValueMetric: time-to-correct-classification of CLAIMED_AGREEMENT versus IMPLEMENTED_GOVERNANCE, plus 3-7 day forecast error for physical-flow normalization
alphaHunter.killCondition: Kill the governance-implementation layer if no public/low-cost operational telemetry can distinguish rhetoric from implementation earlier or more accurately than official statements plus vessel counts.
